oneTimers: $1,890M of restructuring and other charges under Intel's 2025 Restructuring Plan, mostly severance for cutting ~15% of the core workforce; excluded from non-GAAP results and a $(0.45) hit to GAAP EPS.

About $800M of non-cash impairment and accelerated depreciation on excess tools with no identified re-use, plus about $200M of one-time period costs — both sat in cost of sales, cut gross margin by about 800 basis points, and hit GAAP and non-GAAP EPS by about $(0.23) and $(0.20).
A $502M gain on equity investments, net, versus a $(120)M loss a year ago — mark-to-market moves on Intel's investment portfolio rather than chip sales.
otherDetail: Other income of $407M combines a $502M gain on equity investments, net with $(95)M of interest and other, net. Intel recorded a $255M tax provision on a $2,769M pre-tax loss, a (9.2)% GAAP tax rate.

segments.name: Client Computing Group
segments.note: PC and client chips; down 3% YoY on weaker client demand. Segment operating income was $2,053M, down from $2,641M a year ago.

segments.name: Data Center and AI
segments.note: Xeon server chips and AI data-center products; up 4% YoY. Segment operating income was $633M, up from $242M a year ago.

segments.name: Intel Foundry
segments.note: Intel's chip factories, shown at their $22M of sales to OUTSIDE customers only (Q2 2025 10-Q). Foundry's total segment revenue was $4,417M, but $4,395M of that was wafers sold to Intel's own product groups — counting it here would count the same dollars twice. Foundry lost $3,168M in the quarter.

segments.name: All other
segments.note: Mobileye (self-driving tech) and smaller businesses. Intel reports this group at $1,053M; it is shown as $1,027M here, net of $26M of intersegment eliminations not attributable to Foundry, so the parts sum exactly to Intel's $12,859M total. Up 20% YoY.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Jun 28, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Revenue was flat at $12.9B, so the loss came from costs, not sales: $1,890M of restructuring charges (mostly severance for a ~15% workforce cut) plus about $800M of impairments and $200M of one-time period costs. GAAP EPS was $(0.67); non-GAAP EPS was $(0.10).
takeaways.title: A loss driven by restructuring, not sales

takeaways.text: Intel Foundry lost $3,168M on $4,417M of segment revenue, and only $22M of that revenue came from outside customers — the rest was wafers sold to Intel's own product groups. Client Computing still earned $2,053M and Data Center and AI earned $633M.
takeaways.title: Foundry lost more than the whole company

takeaways.text: Adjusted free cash flow was $(1,050)M versus $8,155M a year ago, when partner contributions were $11.4B against $1.3B now. Gross capex was $4.5B. Intel cancelled its planned fabs in Germany and Poland, is consolidating assembly and test in Vietnam and Malaysia, and is slowing construction in Ohio.
takeaways.title: Cash burned while the factories get rebuilt

verdict: Intel lost $2.9 billion in the second quarter as $1.9 billion of restructuring charges and roughly $1 billion of impairments and one-time costs pushed its costs past flat revenue of $12.9 billion, and its chip factories alone lost $3.2 billion.
